label: ENGINEERING_ONLY
comment: G.1b of the T1 node-expansion candidates on TASL-2 (R1-T1-NODE-EXPANSION). Every node value is taken from the reviewed kit record and the U2 census record on main (merge 47d2a39d5). All four censuses ran CPU-only on TASL-2, each on one CPU set, so all four nodes run CPU-only; no GPU card is used. MetaMaze (0-3) and ETTh1 (16-31) run on their census sets; Titanic and Forest Cover were censused on CPUs 8-11, which R1-TASL2-CPU withdraws from every R1 job on TASL-2, so they run on replacement sets of the same size, 12-15 and 4-7 (cpu_replacement), each gated on its fixed-seed determinism check. The four sets are disjoint. Each node's launch is gated in the note (gate_<node>). paper.commit is filled by build_g1bx_launch.py.
note_rule: R1-T1-NODE-EXPANSION (kit -> U2 census on TASL -> G.1b on TASL under a new G.1b note; D21 protocol, 460 runs per node; cap 40 GPU-h; published by the coordinating chat once independently reviewed and its launch checks pass)

harness.comment: each node runs at its own reviewed kit pin (nodes[].harness); all four kits branch from mac-trackg-t1-tasl-20261121 @ c025f89aeafc2199bf3487b4bcaa16678273c702

census.comment: the merge of main-t1-node-expansion-20261125 that published the four kit records, their reviews and the U2 census records; each node binds its own census record by sha256

cpu_preflight.comment: before the attempt and before each part, the job samples /proc/stat for 5 s and refuses if any CPU of the node's CPU set was more than 20 % busy (another job on the set: the G.5 jobs take no CPU lease); the readings go into the job record

caps.comment: all four nodes are CPU nodes: the projection is 0 GPU-h; their CPU core-hours are reported beside it

estimate.comment: the censuses ran on TASL-2 itself, so the ratio is 1.0 (the key keeps the shared name); sensitivity 1.5; MetaMaze and ETTh1 run on their census sets; Titanic and Forest Cover were censused on CPUs 8-11 (cpuinfo_max_freq 6.1 GHz) and run on 5.8 GHz P-core sets (12-15, 4-7), a clock ratio of 6.1/5.8 = 1.052, inside the sensitivity 1.5, and each replacement set's determinism check bounds the node's baseline there at 1.5 x its census B1 (prep report section 5); each job records the measured ratio to the census B1

venv_jax.source: docs/r1/reports/tasl_chain_20261122/METAMAZE_U2_RESULT_20261125_captures/venv_jax.freeze.txt (the census's python -m pip freeze, 56 packages; equal to the kit's MOUNTAINCAR_KIT_20261125_captures/env/venv_jax.freeze.txt)

TASL-2.env_python_comment: the census environments in place, read-only: torch312 (Titanic, ETTh1, Forest Cover) and MetaMaze's venv_jax; each job compares the freeze with the committed census freeze at its start
TASL-2.cpus_comment: cpus 0-7 are TASL-2's GPU-job cpus (no GPU node in this spec); each CPU node runs on its own CPU set: its census set, or its R1-TASL2-CPU replacement; no set contains CPUs 8-11

timeout_decision.authority: R1-G1B-TIMEOUT (census_slowest_x3; the node's own census host TASL-2)

determinism_check.comment: before the node's first job: the census baseline step (s000_baseline, seeds 8001/8001, the census budget) run twice on cpus 12-15 from the node's G.1b checkout at its pin, each in its own 8G/swap-0 scope; PASS when both runs are isolated (effective:true, waivers {}, exceptions []), both result channels have this sha256 (the census baseline's, TITANIC_U2_RESULT_20261125_RETRY_captures/result_channels/s000_baseline.txt, equal to its B2), and each baseline wall time is at most ratio_sensitivity x the census B1; the record's lines are read by the gate (cpu_determinism); prep report section 9

cpu_replacement.comment: census set 8-11 (physical P-cores 4 and 5, 6.1 GHz) withdrawn by R1-TASL2-CPU; 12-15 is one of the sets the TASL-2 CPU stability record passed 3 of 3, bitwise identical (MetaMaze baseline); prep report section 5 gives the choice and the timing basis

disclosures: census: the authorised retry (PASS) on CPUs 8-11; the first attempt on CPUs 16-31 (E-cores) was aborted and the second on 8-11 STOPped with SIGSEGV/SIGILL deaths and a worker death while a sibling smoke shared CPUs 8-11 (TITANIC_U2_RESULT_20261125.md); the G.1b runs on 12-15, its R1-TASL2-CPU replacement set, after that set's fixed-seed determinism check (cpu_replacement)
CPU-only in the kit (mlgym_titanic is in the harness's CPU_ONLY_NODES at 3a67042b, kit record section 3)
the retry record's ceil-based 156 s / 468 s is shown as the raw slowest record 155.965 s / timeout 467.895 s, as every G.1b spec does
kit review c6(i): the tables come from MLGym's pinned commit, not a user Kaggle download

census on CPUs 0-3 (attempt C, PASS); attempts A and B on CPUs 8-11 STOPped with native signals (SIGSEGV rc -11, SIGILL rc -4) after the baseline trained the full budget (METAMAZE_U2_RESULT_20261125.md section 3); the TASL-2 CPU stability record (TASL2_CPU_STABILITY_20261125.md, review ACCEPTED) reproduced the failure on 8-11 (3 of 3) and passed 0-3, 4-7 and 12-15 (3 of 3 each, bitwise identical); R1-TASL2-CPU withdraws 8-11 from every R1 job on TASL-2; MetaMaze stays on 0-3
the kit record is MOUNTAINCAR_KIT_20261125.md (MountainCarContinuous rejected, MetaMaze ported; branch mac-trackg-mountaincar-20261125); there is no separate MetaMaze kit record

mlgym_metamaze is not in the harness's CPU_ONLY_NODES at aa354485 (the kit changes no harness source): the job adds it to autoresearch.trackg.noise_floor.CPU_ONLY_NODES in the engine's own process for its own chunk (census_override); its census driver had added it to tests.trackg.port_smoke_gpu.CPU_ONLY_NODES, the smoke's copy of the list
its census environment venv_jax is not torch312/jax312: the gate needs the PLAN row of decision EXP-ENV containing the admitting sentence verbatim
the data manifest is host-specific (kit review c3/c6(vi)): e2338195 is TASL-2's
census CPU-only on CPUs 16-31 (E-cores), attempt B PASS; attempt A stopped on a launch-environment defect (pinned env not on PATH)
